newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE MUST REVIVE TITLE CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE MUST REVIVE TITLE CHALLENGE.

text.p: Pre-season favourite Jacques Villeneuve believes complacency has cost his Williams team dearly and that he now has his work cut out to revive his title challenge in the British Grand Prix on Sunday.
Villeneuve has fallen off the pace in recent weeks allowing Michael Schumacher in a Ferrari to steal a 14-point advantage in the world driver's championship.

"This is obviously a very important race for us," said Villeneuve. "But I am reasonably confident. We went well in testing at Silverstone and I feel sure we can achieve a good result. We need one because we have to cut the gap."

Villeneuve, who has gone two races without a win, leads the Williams challenge for their 100th grand prix victory at the same high-speed circuit where his father Gilles made his Formula One debut 20 years ago.

"We went very well at the start of the year, perhaps too well," the Canadian said. "It meant the team started to concentrate on next year's car, the 1998 one with the new regulations, instead of working on developing the new one.
"I think maybe we got caught out because it allowed Ferrari in particular to catch us up. Now we have got our work cut out to stay in the fight and it is important we do well at Silverstone."

While Villeneuve plots a comeback on Williams 'home' track, the closest to their Grove base in Oxfordshire, Schumacher will be aiming for a third successive victory to cement his challenge for a third world title in four years.
"I have never won at Silverstone," said Schumacher. "That is something I would like to correct as soon as I can.
"For me, it would be something special to win at Silverstone, but of course it would also be another big boost to my championship chances."

Schumacher said he did not expect to lead by 14 points at the halfway stage to the season, but admitted: "The team has made fantastic progress with the car in recent weeks, both in reliability and performance. I was surprised how competitive we were in France and if we can maintain that then I hope to win more races this year than I expected.
"If I can do that, then there is no reason why I cannot win the championship. And that would be really fantastic."

Schumacher knows that he faces a formidable challenge this weekend from both Williams drivers as the Anglo-French team seeks a one-two triumph to close the gap in the constructors' and drivers' series.
"That is what we have to do to keep Ferrari within reach -- we cannot let the gap increase," said team chief Frank Williams.
This year's British race takes place on a revised 5.140-km track which is expected to provide the fastest race of the season so far.

"I think it is a good compromise between speed and safety and I expect our Williams-Renault car to go well there," said Villeneuve's team mate Heinz-Harald Frentzen. "I really hope I can bring the team their 100th win on the track where they won their first."
